facts: Running OCX in CI has one core challenge: shell environment changes do not cross step boundaries. [L6]
A fresh process in the next step resets PATH and loses variables, so packages installed in step one are invisible. [L8]
ocx env --ci and ocx package env --ci write the composed environment into the CI system's persistence channel. [L10]
--shell exports lines for the current step only, while --ci makes the environment available to every later step. [L13]
GITHUB_PATH entries are prepended to PATH for later steps, so OCX package directories land leftmost. [L20]
GITHUB_ENV receives KEY=VALUE lines, with heredoc blocks for multiline values, exported to all later steps. [L21]
ocx env --ci=github reads the runner's file paths from its own variables and appends the results directly, with no jq. [L23]
Only the literal PATH variable goes to GITHUB_PATH; other path variables go to GITHUB_ENV with OCX directories prepended. [L25]
List-type variables also go to GITHUB_ENV, but OCX appends their contribution instead of prepending it. [L25]
Running --ci=github outside a GitHub Actions runner exits 78, a configuration error. [L27]
The setup-ocx action installs OCX and replays the project toolchain from ocx.lock, pinned by commit SHA in the example. [L31]
The turnkey workflow example runs cmake and ninja version checks after the setup step. [L33]
A bare --ci also auto-detects GitHub Actions, because the runner sets GITHUB_ACTIONS to true. [L95]
--ci=gitlab targets the GitLab step runner, is experimental, and is incompatible with traditional script jobs. [L100]
The step runner persists variables through an export file, with one JSON object per line. [L102]
ocx env --ci=gitlab writes that JSON-lines format to the export file or to stdout when none is given. [L108]
GitLab flattens path entries into one joined value, prepending package directories to the current PATH. [L110]
The export file persists variables to later steps within the same job, not across separate jobs. [L115]
Traditional script jobs cannot read the JSON format, and OCX does not emit the dotenv format they need. [L117]
Without --export-file, output goes to stdout, which must be redirected with an append to the export file. [L143]
With --export-file OCX opens the file in append mode, so no redirect is needed. [L150]
